title: Qingyao's Secret Report
next_chapter_hook: The jade pendant in his palm emitted a cold, dim glow, the ancient rune patterns seeming to squirm like living things—and Chen Ji faintly sensed an inexplicable tremor from deep within the Tianji Record.

text.content: The footsteps outside the window were so light they nearly merged with the night wind; had Chen Ji not honed his perception to be as careful as walking on thin ice over these years, he would have almost overlooked them. He didn't look up, merely folding the secret letter in his hand slowly, his movements unhurried, as if completely unaware of that watching gaze. One of Third Elder's people? Or something else? Various possibilities flashed through his mind as his fingertips unconsciously traced the outline of the cinnabar seal's impression at the edge of the paper, the pine-ink's distinctive bitter fragrance still lingering at his nostrils. The candlelight in the room swayed, stretching his shadow alternately long and short, much like the lurking killing intent behind this letter.

dialogue.content: "Don't move." A barely audible hiss came from the direction of the window, followed by a slender figure silently flitting in like a falling leaf, carrying a faint winter plum fragrance. "It's me."

text.content: Chen Ji looked up to see Su Qingyao dressed in night operations attire, her black hair tied back. The usual cold arrogance between her brows had diminished somewhat, replaced by a gravity he had never witnessed before. Her breathing was slightly rapid, fine beads of sweat on her temples, clearly indicating her journey here had not been easy. Yet what truly stirred Chen Ji's heart was the un-concealable anxiety deep within her eyes—this woman who always looked down on others, when had she ever been so distraught? He slowly tucked the secret letter into his sleeve, a timid smile surfacing on his face as usual, his voice pressed very low.

dialogue.content: "Senior Su, what important matter brings you here so late at night?" He deliberately made his voice tremble more, as if greatly startled. "If others were to see..."

"No time for pretenses." Su Qingyao frowned, her gaze like a blade sweeping over his cowering expression. The corner of her mouth twitched slightly, seemingly both resigned and somewhat accustomed. "In half an hour, three from the Demonic Path will infiltrate from the eastern edge of the Forbidden Grounds. One of them is... a hidden agent of the Holy Sect."

text.content: Chen Ji's lowered lashes trembled slightly. The eastern edge of the Forbidden Grounds—that was exactly the area he had vaguely sensed while deducing the Tianji Record yesterday—though the vision then had been too hazy, he had dismissed it as ordinary abnormal activity and hadn't thought deeply about it. A hidden agent of the Holy Sect... No one understood the weight of these three words better than him. He didn't immediately respond, instead slowly standing up, staggering two steps before stabilizing, looking completely like someone whose legs had given out from fear. Yet in those lowered eyes, a dark light had quietly begun to circulate.

dialogue.content: "You—" Su Qingyao seemed angered by his useless appearance, but the next moment she took a deep breath, forcing back the rebuke on her lips. "I know you're no ordinary person, but I've never intended to expose you. As for tonight's information, believe it or not."

text.content: She paused, her gaze fixed directly on Chen Ji's extremely ordinary face, as if trying to extract some truth from it: "I'll only ask you one thing—when the great purge arrives, will you kill innocents without restraint?" This question came abruptly. Chen Ji looked up at her, only to see a hint of earnestness appearing in this usually cold and proud woman's eyes. Alarm bells rang in his heart: Su Qingyao never spoke without purpose, there must be deeper meaning behind her question.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao's late-night visit brought extremely critical intelligence, but she was also testing Chen Ji's bottom line. As a schemer who walked the world under the guise of a useless person, Chen Ji had to decide how to respond to this question touching upon his true nature.

choices.text: "The innocent bear no guilt—I certainly will not."
choices.description: Responding to Su Qingyao's test directly, giving a commitment. This will make her trust you more, but also exposes your code of conduct.
choices.risk_hint: She may use this as leverage

dialogue.content: A flash of surprise crossed Su Qingyao's eyes, then transformed into a very faint sense of relief. She slightly nodded, the coldness in her voice softening somewhat: "I knew I wasn't mistaken about you."

text.content: She took out a jade pendant from her bosom and handed it to Chen Ji. The pendant was warm and smooth as water, but the runes carved upon it exuded an ancient, desolate aura—ritual patterns that existed only in high antiquity, entirely different from the schools of today's cultivation world. The moment Chen Ji received the jade pendant, a slight tingling sensation spread through his fingertips, as if something had slipped into his body along with that coolness.

choices.description: Not answering directly, but instead asking why she cares about this matter. Testing her true intentions while concealing your own attitude.
choices.risk_hint: She may feel you don't trust her

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao's expression stiffened for a moment, then she smiled self-deprecatingly: "As expected, you're still this suspicious. Very well... I simply don't want to see innocent people become sacrifices in sect struggles."

choices.description: Neither making promises nor asking questions, applying pressure through silence to force her to voluntarily reveal more information.
choices.visible_cost: The atmosphere grew even more tense
choices.risk_hint: She might leave because of this

text.content: A suffocating silence filled the room. The candlelight flickered between the two, stretching Su Qingyao's shadow long and short. She pressed her lips tightly together, her gaze flickering with struggle, disappointment, finally crystallizing into a hint of resolve: 'Forget it... I shouldn't have come.'

dialogue.content: 'The source of this intelligence, you need not inquire about.' Su Qingyao took a deep breath, her voice extremely low, 'But I can tell you—this person... has an old connection with me.' As she spoke these words, a faint trace of sorrow flickered in her eyes, vanishing in an instant.

text.content: Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, his mind racing. Su Qingyao has an old connection with the Demonic Holy Sect? This information was like a blade, cutting open a gap in his originally vague understanding. He recalled her unusually familiar reactions to demonic matters in their daily interactions, the precise judgments she occasionally revealed about the Holy Sect's internal structure... This woman's identity was likely far more complex than he had imagined. Yet he did not probe further, merely placing the Jade Pendant into his chest, his fingertip caressing the cold runes inscribed upon it, a silent warning echoing in his heart: accepting this object means incurring a debt of gratitude.

dialogue.content: 'The one I wish you to protect is an Outer Disciple named Shen Qing.' Su Qingyao's voice carried a hint of plea, 'With the Great Purification imminent, his name was maliciously added to the purge list. While those who truly deserve death... still go unpunished.'

text.content: Shen Qing. Chen Ji quickly searched through his memory for this name. An Outer Disciple and menial servant, with mediocre talent, usually silent and reserved, practically without any presence. How could such a person be placed on the purge list? He immediately sensed something was amiss—someone wanted to kill by proxy, and this 'blade' was none other than the turbulent times of the Sect's Great Purification. A faint cold smile tugged at the corner of Chen Ji's mouth. This was the familiar game he knew well—every shift of power always required some people to become scapegoats.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao requested Chen Ji to protect an innocent person named Shen Qing during the Great Purification. This request touched upon a hidden thread in Chen Ji's secret scheme to manipulate the world—he needed to decide whether to expend energy on this chess piece.

choices.risk_hint: Shen Qing's identity may not be simple

dialogue.content: 'I'll handle it.' Chen Ji's voice was calm, without the slightest fluctuation, 'But Su Senior Sister, this favor I have noted.'

choices.visible_reward: Obtain higher value intelligence or promise

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao was stunned for a moment, then snorted coldly: 'You've become more like a merchant indeed. Speak, what do you want?'

choices.description: Refuse to take on this matter. Protecting an insignificant menial servant would only disrupt his carefully arranged chess game.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao's face instantly chilled. She stared at Chen Ji for a long moment, then suddenly let out a cold laugh: 'What a heartless Chen shidi. Consider tonight's matter as if I never said it.'

text.content: Night wind rose outside the window, making the window lattice creak. Faint footsteps of patrolling disciples came from afar, and Su Qingyao's expression grew increasingly tense. She drew from her sleeve a piece of silk as thin as a cicada's wing, densely covered in tiny characters—the infiltrator's route and ambush points. This intelligence alone was worth bankrupting any minor sect.

'Three days later, at the third watch of the Zi hour, someone will provide support at the withered well on the edge of the eastern Forbidden Grounds.' Su Qingyao pressed the silk into Chen Ji's hand, her voice urgent. 'The Holy Sect's hidden operative will swap identity tokens at the support point, then blend into the crowds attending the Sect Competition. This person's cultivation has reached mid Core Formation stage, skilled at concealing their aura—ordinary detection techniques won't find them.' She paused, fixing Chen Ji with an intense stare. 'This is all I've uncovered. How to proceed... that's entirely for you to decide.'

Chen Ji tucked the silk into his sleeve, his fingertips discreetly stroking the cool fabric. Three days later, third watch, by the withered well. He closed his eyes, his mind racing. The Tianji Record's Foresight Ability was useless here—he couldn't waste precious chances on something so trivial. Yet with this intelligence, he already had seventy percent certainty to lay a perfect trap. The remaining thirty percent variable was Su Qingyao herself—where did her intelligence come from? What was her relationship with that Holy Sect operative? Why would she betray her position to help him?

dialogue.content: 'I know what you're thinking.' Su Qingyao suddenly spoke, her voice carrying a thread of exhaustion. 'My origins, you'll eventually know. But not now.' She turned, her slender back looking especially fragile in the candlelight. 'I can only say... my mother died at the hands of the Holy Sect. And that infiltrator—that was one of the executioners.'

text.content: This sentence was like a boulder dropped into a calm lake, stirring up layers of ripples. Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, and another crucial piece of the puzzle fell into place—so that's how it was. Su Qingyao's knowledge of the Demonic Path wasn't unfounded; between her and the Holy Sect lay a blood feud. If this identity were exposed, her position in the sect would instantly crumble. Yet she was willing to risk this danger to deliver such classified intelligence to him... the weight of this trust had exceeded simple transactional interests.

Su Qingyao turned her head, those usually cold eyes now brimming with complex emotions—hatred, unwillingness, and a hint of vulnerability. 'I don't ask for your trust now, only that you remember tonight's words.' She took a deep breath, her voice recovering its usual coldness. 'The matter three days from now, you'll decide yourself. This is all I can do.' With that, she turned to climb out the window.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao is about to leave, and secrets seem to still hide behind that Jade Pendant and the 'ancient runes' she mentioned. As a strategist, Chen Ji needs to decide whether to pursue this matter.

choices.text: Inquire about the Jade Pendant's origins
choices.description: The runes on that Jade Pendant were peculiar. Chen Ji decided to ask for clarification before she left. This might be the key to unraveling the mystery of her identity.
choices.risk_hint: She may be unwilling to disclose

dialogue.content: 'This Jade Pendant...' Chen Ji spoke, his voice still carrying a hint of timidity. 'May Su shimei clarify?'

text.content: Su Qingyao's footsteps halted. She glanced back, a meaningful curve forming at the corner of her lips: 'This is the only keepsake my mother left me. The runes inscribed on it are... the inheritance mark of an ancient bloodline.' Her voice dropped extremely low. 'In critical moments, it might save your life.'

choices.description: No further questions, keeping this favor in your heart. Sometimes, knowing too much is a burden.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain a sense of mystery, letting her take the initiative to approach

text.content: Chen Ji did not pursue the question, only giving a slight nod as he watched that slender figure vanish like a specter into the night. The candle flame burned lonely behind him, stretching his shadow impossibly long. He slowly sat back at the desk, taking the Jade Pendant from his chest and examining it carefully under the candlelight. The runes flickered in and out of visibility between light and shadow, emanating an ancient aura that inspired heart-trembling fear—that was an existence beyond the current cultivation world. His fingertips gently traced the runes, and suddenly an inexplicable tremor rose in his heart, as if something was awakening deep within the Tianji Record.

Night wind slipped through the window cracks, making the candle flame shudder violently. At that moment, Chen Ji heard a faint humming from his chest—the unique vibration of the Tianji Record Fragment. His heart tightened, and he quickly probed his consciousness into the Mental Sea. The yellowed pages glowed faintly, and several blurred lines of text faintly emerged at the edges: 'Heavenly fate's vessel, inherited by hidden bloodlines...' The text beyond was too blurry; no matter how intently he focused, he couldn't see clearly. He withdrew his spiritual sense, his gaze falling on the Jade Pendant in his palm. He already had a plan in his heart—Su Qingyao's identity was likely far more than just 'Inner Disciple Senior Fellow.' And this keepsake left by her mother might be the key to unlocking all of this.

Moonlight like water draped over Tianqing Sect, enveloping it in serene tranquility. From afar, the bell tower delivered three muffled chimes—the Zi hour had passed. Chen Ji tucked the Jade Pendant into his chest, rose, and walked to the window. His gaze pierced through layers of rooftops, looking toward the eastern Forbidden Grounds. The interests and losses of the situation three days later—he had already seen through them all. Su Qingyao's intelligence, the Holy Sect's hidden operative, the chaos of the purification—all these would become the newest pieces on his chessboard. And he, Chen Ji, would eventually crush all the ants daring to peek in the shadows into powder.
